outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL AFFECT CENTRAL AND EASTERN PARTS OF VIRGINA AND NORTH CAROLINA THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. LARGE HAIL...CORRIDORS OF WIND DAMAGE AND A FEW TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE LARGE-SCALE PATTERN WILL UNDERGO AMPLIFICATION DURING THE DAY ONE PERIOD IN RESPONSE TO THE EQUATORWARD PROGRESSION OF 100+ KT MID AND UPPER-LEVEL JET STREAKS JUST OFF THE CA COAST...AND THE SUBSEQUENT INTENSIFICATION OF A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH OVER THE WRN STATES. DOWNSTREAM FROM THESE DEVELOPMENTS...A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH OVER THE OH/TN VALLEYS WILL SLOWLY WEAKEN WHILE TRANSLATING EWD TO OFF THE MID-ATLANTIC COAST BY TONIGHT...AHEAD OF AN UPPER LOW SHIFTING SEWD ACROSS THE GREAT LAKES. AT THE SURFACE...LOW PRESSURE ASSOCIATED WITH THE OH/TN VALLEY IMPULSE WILL UNDERGO OCCLUSION AND GRADUAL WEAKENING AS IT DEVELOPS FROM CNTRL IND INTO UPSTATE NY. THE DEVELOPMENT AND SUBSEQUENT DEEPENING OF A SECONDARY LOW IS ANTICIPATED BY AFTERNOON AT THE INTERSECTION OF A LEE TROUGH AND NWD-MOVING WARM FRONT OVER N-CNTRL NC/S-CNTRL VA WITH THIS FEATURE TRACKING OFF THE DE/SRN NJ COAST BY TONIGHT. MEANWHILE...A COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE EWD THROUGH THE UPPER OH VALLEY AND LOWER GREAT LAKES WITH THE SRN EXTENSION OF THIS BOUNDARY PROGRESSING EWD THROUGH THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS TO OFF THE MIDDLE AND SRN ATLANTIC COAST BY 26/12Z.

sections.title: MID-ATLANTIC STATES THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING
sections.text: THE MASS RESPONSE TO THE ABOVE-MENTIONED MIGRATORY SHORT-WAVE TROUGH WILL MAINTAIN A SLY/SWLY LLJ OVER THE PIEDMONT AND COASTAL PLAIN TODAY WHICH IN TURN WILL PROMOTE THE POLEWARD FLUX OF AN INCREASINGLY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER EAST OF THE LEE TROUGH. THIS MOISTENING COUPLED WITH STEEPENING MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND DAYTIME HEATING WILL YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS WITHIN THE NWD-EXPANDING WARM SECTOR WITH AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 1000-1500 J/KG. SURFACE-BASED STORM DEVELOPMENT IS ANTICIPATED BY EARLY AFTERNOON ALONG THE LEE TROUGH OVER CNTRL PARTS OF VA/NC AS MIDLEVEL HEIGHT FALLS/DCVA SPREAD EAST OF THE APPALACHIANS. LATEST CONVECTION-ALLOWING MODEL GUIDANCE INDICATES THE UPSCALE GROWTH OF STORMS INTO A CONVECTIVE BAND COMPRISED OF BOWING AND SUPERCELL STRUCTURES OWING TO THE PRESENCE OF 40-50 KT OF WSWLY DEEP-LAYER SHEAR. LARGE HAIL AND CORRIDORS OF WIND DAMAGE APPEAR TO BE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS WITH THESE STORMS INTO THIS EVENING. HOWEVER...STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL SHEAR THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING OVER ERN NC/SERN VA WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF A FEW TORNADOES WITH ANY LONGER-LIVED ROTATING STORMS.

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: CURRENT BAND OF ELEVATED TSTMS FROM SRN OH TO NERN TN IS INDICATIVE OF VIGOROUS FORCING FOR ASCENT ACCOMPANYING THE SHORT-WAVE TROUGH. THIS ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY PERSIST TODAY WITH SOME INTENSIFICATION POSSIBLE -NAMELY ALONG THE COLD FRONT- AS THE MIDLEVEL COLD POOL COMBINES WITH DAYTIME HEATING TO YIELD WEAK INSTABILITY. ISOLATED OCCURRENCES OF SMALL HAIL AND/OR LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON. ..MEAD/MOSIER.. 04/25/2014

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL AFFECT CENTRAL AND EASTERN PARTS OF VIRGINA AND NORTH CAROLINA THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. SEVERAL TORNADOES...CORRIDORS OF WIND DAMAGE...AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: CENTRAL AND ERN NC/VA THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING
sections.text: A COMPACT SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED SURFACE COLD FRONT/TROUGH WILL MOVE EWD FROM THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS TO THE MID ATLANTIC COAST BY EARLY TONIGHT. IN ADVANCE OF THE SURFACE FRONT/TROUGH...LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE IS INCREASING RAPIDLY ACROSS CENTRAL/ERN NC AND WILL CONTINUE TO SPREAD NWD TOWARD THE VA BORDER THIS AFTERNOON. STRONG SURFACE HEATING IS ALSO ONGOING ACROSS THE CAROLINAS TO THE E OF AN ERODING STRATUS DECK OVER THE NC PIEDMONT...WHICH WILL CONTRIBUTE TO MODERATE BUOYANCY /MLCAPE NEAR 1500 J PER KG/ THIS AFTERNOON IN THE WARM SECTOR. TWO MODES OF CONVECTIVE INITIATION ARE EXPECTED TODAY - A FEW DISCRETE CELLS IN THE DESTABILIZING WARM SECTOR BY EARLY-MID AFTERNOON...AND A BAND OF STORMS ALONG THE CONSOLIDATING COLD FRONT/LEE TROUGH BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON INVOF CENTRAL NC. IN CONJUNCTION WITH THE WARM SECTOR DESTABILIZATION...VERTICAL SHEAR WILL ALSO BECOME FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELLS. THE SEASONABLY RICH MOISTURE AND MODERATE BUOYANCY...ALONG WITH EFFECTIVE SRH OF 200-300 M2/S2...WILL SUPPORT A RISK FOR SEVERAL TORNADOES...INCLUDING AN ISOLATED STRONG TORNADO THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING.

sections.title: UPPER OH VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: WIDESPREAD CLOUDS WILL TEND TO LIMIT SURFACE HEATING/DESTABILIZATION ACROSS THE UPPER OH VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON. HOWEVER...IF POCKETS OF HEATING CAN DEVELOP IN SMALL CLOUD BREAKS NOTED IN VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY IMMEDIATELY IN ADVANCE OF THE MIDLEVEL WAVE...THERE COULD BE SOME RISK FOR ISOLATED STRONG/DAMAGING GUSTS AND SMALL HAIL FOR A FEW HOURS THIS AFTERNOON.

sections.title: ELSEWHERE
sections.text: A STRONG MIDLEVEL TROUGH WILL MOVE INLAND OVER CA LATER TODAY...AND REACH THE LOWER CO RIVER VALLEY BY EARLY SATURDAY. COLD MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES AND MOIST PROFILES WILL SUPPORT WEAK INSTABILITY AND AN ISOLATED THUNDERSTORM RISK FROM THE CENTRAL CA COAST INTO THE NRN GREAT BASIN. OTHERWISE...MOISTENING ABOVE THE SURFACE IN A WAA REGIME COULD SUPPORT ELEVATED THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT EARLY SATURDAY MORNING INVOF ERN KS/WRN MO. ..THOMPSON/DEAN.. 04/25/2014

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WILL AFFECT CENTRAL AND EASTERN PARTS OF VIRGINA AND NORTH CAROLINA THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. SEVERAL TORNADOES...CORRIDORS OF WIND DAMAGE...AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: 20Z UPDATE
sections.text: ENVIRONMENT IS INCREASINGLY FAVORABLE OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS /ESPECIALLY 20Z TO 00Z/ FOR TORNADOES...ONE OR TWO OF WHICH MAY BE STRONG...MAINLY ACROSS PORTIONS OF EAST-CENTRAL/NORTHEAST NC INTO SOUTHEAST VA. COINCIDENT WITH A MAXIMIZED CORRIDOR OF SURFACE PRESSURE FALLS /1-2 MB PER HR/...THE RALEIGH AND PARTICULARLY THE WAKEFIELD WSR-88D VWP/S HAVE SHOWN A STEADY INCREASE IN LOW-LEVEL SRH OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS AS NEAR-SURFACE WINDS REMAIN BACKED /SOUTHEASTERLY/. THIS IS WHILE LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE HAS INCREASED /MAINLY LOWER 60S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS/. REFERENCE TORNADO WATCH 91 AND MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 403/404 FOR ADDITIONAL SHORT-TERM DETAILS. ..GUYER.. 04/25/2014 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1108 AM CDT FRI APR 25 2014/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE RISK FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS INCLUDING TORNADOES WILL INCREASE DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS...AND A TORNADO WATCH WILL LIKELY BE ISSUED DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS OR SO.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC OBS INDICATE LOWER/MIDDLE 60S SFC DEWPOINTS SPREADING NWD OVER THE NC/VA PIEDMONT AND COASTAL PLAIN IN ADVANCE OF A POTENT MID/UPPER PV MAX CROSSING THE CNTRL/SRN APPALACHIANS. DIURNAL HEATING HAS CONTRIBUTED TO MLCAPE AROUND 1500 J/KG S OF A NWD-RETREATING WARM FRONT ANALYZED FROM SRN VA TO NERN NC. INCREASINGLY AGITATED BOUNDARY-LAYER CU AND INCIPIENT CONVECTION OVER THE COASTAL PLAIN SUGGEST THAT WARM-SECTOR INHIBITION IS LIMITED...AND STORMS SHOULD INCREASE IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY ACROSS THE AREA AS DEEP ASCENT PRECEDING THE PV MAX AND ITS ASSOCIATED COLD FRONT SPREAD ACROSS THE AREA. FURTHERMORE... STRENGTHENING MID-LEVEL FLOW/DEEP SHEAR -- E.G. AROUND 50 KT 0-6-KM BULK SHEAR PER FCX VWP -- WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORM MODES...INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND CONVECTIVE CLUSTERS/BOWING SEGMENTS WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL. LONG/CURVED LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ENCOURAGED BY RELATIVELY BACKED SFC WINDS -- PARTICULARLY ALONG/E OF A DEVELOPING LEE TROUGH OVER THE PIEDMONT -- WILL YIELD THE RISK FOR TORNADOES.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LOW RISK FOR ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS CANNOT BE RULED OUT THIS AFTERNOON. WHILE CONVECTIVE TRENDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE MONITORED...THE ISSUANCE OF A WW IS CURRENTLY UNLIKELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE CURRENT/ANTICIPATED TRAJECTORY OF A COMPACT MID-LEVEL VORT MAX EMERGING OVER THE VA/NC PIEDMONT SUGGESTS THAT POLEWARD LOW-LEVEL MASS FLUXES CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING MORE ROBUST BUOYANCY WILL REMAIN RELEGATED TO TORNADO WATCH 91. FARTHER NORTH...LOW-LEVEL SLYS WILL SUPPORT THE INFLUX OF MORE MODEST LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE -- E.G. LOW/MID 50S SFC DEWPOINTS. WEAK BOUNDARY-LAYER DESTABILIZATION MAY ENSUE...THOUGH THIS IS BEING STUNTED BY A MID/HIGH-LEVEL CANOPY CAST DOWNSTREAM OF ONGOING CONVECTION ENTERING THE LEE OF THE APPALACHIANS. REGARDLESS...WITH STRONG DEEP FORCING FOR ASCENT/SHEAR SPREADING ACROSS THE AREA DURING THE PEAK OF THE DIURNAL HEATING CYCLE...STRONG STORMS WITH GUSTY WINDS AND PERHAPS SMALL HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE. A DMGG WIND GUST OR POSSIBLY A TORNADO CANNOT BE ENTIRELY RULED OUT... PARTICULARLY FOR LOCATIONS JUST NORTH OF TORNADO WATCH 91 FROM CNTRL VA TO E-CNTRL VA.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE TORNADO POTENTIAL IS INCREASING ACROSS PARTS OF THE PIEDMONT AND COASTAL PLAIN OF NORTH CAROLINA AND SRN VIRGINIA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC MESOANALYSIS REVELS A WWD-ADVANCING AGGREGATE OUTFLOW/SEA BREEZE BOUNDARY RUNNING ROUGHLY FROM HALIFAX TO CUMBERLAND COUNTY. AS ONGOING DISCRETE/SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS EVOLVING OVER THE PIEDMONT SPREAD E INTO THE MOISTER/MODERATELY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT EAST OF THIS BOUNDARY...THEY WILL ENCOUNTER RELATIVELY BACKED SFC WINDS TO BOOST EFFECTIVE SRH TO AROUND 200 M2/S2. LOW-LEVEL HELICITY WILL FURTHER INCREASE AS STRONGER DEEP FLOW ARRIVES IN ASSOCIATION WITH AN ACCOMPANYING PV MAX AND LOW-LEVEL FLOW RESPONDS. TRENDS IN RAX VWP DATA ALREADY REFLECT THIS RESPONSE. AS SUCH...THE RISK FOR TORNADOES WILL INCREASE IN THE NEAR-TERM...PARTICULARLY IN ERN NC AND SERN VA. A STRONG TORNADO RISK WILL EXIST. ..COHEN.. 04/25/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE RISK FOR TORNADOES...DAMAGING WINDS,..AND LARGE HAIL CONTINUES ACROSS TORNADO WATCH 91.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE GREATEST TORNADO RISK WILL AFFECT PARTS OF THE NRN COASTAL PLAIN OF NC AND ADJACENT PARTS OF THE TIDEWATER OF VA DURING THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS...AND ONE OR TWO STRONG TORNADOES CANNOT BE RULED OUT. VIS IMAGERY DEPICTS CONFLUENCE OF BOUNDARY-LAYER CLOUD STREETS EXTENDING NWD INTO A LARGER MASS OF SEMI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS ACROSS CNTRL/N-CNTRL NC...HIGHLIGHTING MODERATELY UNSTABLE INFLOW INGESTED INTO THE ONGOING STORMS. MHX AND AKQ VWPS SAMPLE LONG/CURVED LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS SUPPORTING 150-250 0-1-KM SRH...AND LOW-LEVEL SRH SHOULD INCREASE FURTHER AS TROPOSPHERIC FLOW FIELDS RESPOND AHEAD OF AN APPROACHING MID-LEVEL VORT MAX...REINFORCING THE TORNADO RISK AS STORMS SPREAD E. ELSEWHERE...SFC OBS REVEAL 2-HRLY PRESSURE FALLS AROUND 2.0-3.5 MB...REFLECTING THE STRENGTHENING DEEP ASCENT THAT WILL PROMPT AN INCREASE IN CONVECTIVE COVERAGE OVER THE PIEDMONT DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH THE RISK FOR SVR STORMS. ..COHEN.. 04/25/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE RISK FOR TORNADOES CONTINUES WITHIN THE ERN HALF OF WATCH 91 FROM ERN NC INTO SERN VA...ESPECIALLY WITH ANY DISCRETE STORMS ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR NWD INTO SERN VA. MEANWHILE...STORMS CONSOLIDATING INTO A LINE NEAR THE COLD FRONT SHOULD ENHANCE THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS FROM W-E ACROSS ERN NC AND FAR SERN VA. TIMING OF THIS LINE OF STORMS SUGGESTS THE SEVERE WEATHER THREAT OVER FAR ERN NC AND FAR SERN VA WILL NOT END UNTIL AFTER 02-03Z...SUCH THAT A LOCAL WFO TEMPORAL EXTENSION OF THIS WATCH MAY BE NEEDED FROM THE COASTAL COUNTIES TO THE OUTER BANKS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: OBJECTIVE ANALYSES INDICATED THE PARAMETER SPACE ACROSS ERN NC INTO SERN VA REMAINED SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED STORMS WITH ROTATING UPDRAFTS. LOW LEVEL SRH RANGING FROM 300-400+ M2/S2 FROM AKQ TO MHX...RESPECTIVELY...CONTINUES TO ENHANCE THE TORNADIC POTENTIAL WITH ANY OF THE PRE-COLD FRONTAL DISCRETE STORMS. MEANWHILE...REGIONAL RADAR IMAGERY SHOWED DURING THE LAST HOUR /SINCE 2225Z/ A LINE OF STORMS HAD DEVELOPED ALONG AND JUST EAST OF A COLD FRONT WHICH TRAILED SSWWD FROM THE SURFACE LOW CENTERED NEAR RZZ /ROANOKE RAPIDS NC/. 40-45 KT WLY LOW LEVEL WINDS AT 0.5-1 KM AGL PER RAH WSR-88D WITHIN THE SRN HALF OF THE COMPACT SHORTWAVE TROUGH MOVING EWD ACROSS SRN VA WILL ENHANCE THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS ALONG THIS LINE OF STORMS. BOWING STRUCTURES...SIMILAR TO THE ONE EXTENDING FROM BERTIE COUNTY TO NRN PITT COUNTY...WILL BE LIKELY AS THIS LINE OF STORMS ADVANCES EWD AT 40-45 KT...REACHING THE COAST BETWEEN 0130-03Z. ..PETERS.. 04/25/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A BAND OF THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE REGION THROUGH MID MORNING...BUT SEVERE WEATHER POTENTIAL APPEARS LIKELY TO REMAIN LOW TO NEGLIGIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: IN THE PRESENCE OF VERY STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...MOISTURE RETURN TO A DEVELOPING ZONE OF LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION HAS CONTRIBUTED TO SUFFICIENT DESTABILIZATION FOR AN EVOLVING BAND OF THUNDERSTORM ACTIVITY. CONVECTION APPEARS GENERALLY FOCUSED ALONG THE THERMAL GRADIENT AROUND THE 700 MB LEVEL...DELINEATING THE LEADING EDGE OF A WARMING AND MORE STRONGLY CAPPING MID-LEVEL ENVIRONMENT. THIS IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE SPREADING NORTH NORTHEASTWARD TOWARD THE LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY THROUGH THE 12-15Z TIME. ALTHOUGH STRONGEST CORES HAVE BEEN OCCASIONALLY INCREASING IN INTENSITY...AND PERHAPS ACCOMPANIED BY SMALL HAIL...CAPE APPEARS LIKELY TO REMAIN GENERALLY WEAK...WITH CLOUD BEARING LAYER SHEAR ALSO WEAK TO MODEST IN STRENGTH AT BEST THROUGH MID MORNING. AS A RESULT...LITTLE SUBSTANTIAL FURTHER STRENGTHENING OF CONVECTION IS ANTICIPATED...WITH STORMS LIKELY TO REMAIN SUB-SEVERE.
